summary: web-AI action readiness gate — never act on a page that is not demonstrably ready; post-action never assumed
implementation: src/shared/action-readiness.ts (pure): ordered READINESS_GATES chain (NAVIGATION_ACCEPTED → DOM_READY → TARGET_EXISTS → TARGET_VISIBLE → TARGET_ENABLED → TARGET_STABLE → ACTION_ALLOWED), readinessFromProbe verdict with blockers, postActionVerified (fail-closed: no observed change ⇒ unverified), escalationAfterFailure (bounded retry → selector refresh → alternate strategy)

electron/computer/backends/dom-page.ts: DomBackendOptions.preflightReadiness — before ANY high-risk action (click_control/enter_text/submit) a bounded readiness probe (DOM ready/target exists/visible/enabled/stable) must pass, else the action is refused with the blocking gates listed (no premature mutation)
electron/computer/provider-page-repair.ts: the Computer-Use repair executor enables the readiness gate by default (override false only for deterministic ready-mocks)
tests: tests/unit/action-readiness.test.ts (+5): chain order; ready probe no blockers; loading/invisible blocks with gates; post-action verification fail-closed; bounded escalation

tests/unit/provider-page-repair.test.ts: REPAIRED plan runs readiness before the mutation (script order); not-ready page ⇒ FAILED with NO click action executed; page becoming ready within the bounded window proceeds; DENIED/UNCERTAIN/failure paths preserved
notes: Readiness is wired default-on into the DOM-tier Computer-Use repair chain (production seam). ProviderAutomation/WebRecovery readiness remains a live-area follow-up tied to R-202.
